title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + RoPE/rotary + KV/continuous-batching
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token latency and peak GPU memory for long-context workloads while keeping numerical correctness and providing a safe rollout path. This PR upgrades our attention kernels to a FlashAttentionV2-based implementation with several fused operator optimizations, explicit RoPE/rotary compatibility layers, and KV-cache layout changes that enable lower-copy continuous batching. The change addresses three recurring issues observed in production: 1) tail latency spikes for long sequences when using the previous attention kernels, 2) excessive memory allocation during KV cache flushes, and 3) suboptimal batching for mixed sequence-length traffic.

What this PR does (summary):
- Integrates FlashAttentionV2 kernels with our kernel selector and runtime fallbacks. Kernels are chosen based on model head size, sequence-length distribution, and hardware capability.
- Adds fused-op paths for softmax+dropout and qk scaling+softmax to reduce intermediate allocations.
- Implements a rotary embedding codepath fused with attention matmul for rotary-based models and preserves RoPE semantics for models that use explicit RoPE. Includes conversion tests between rotary and RoPE to ensure parity.
- Reworks KV-cache memory layout (compact contiguous layout with optional pinned buffers) to reduce CUDA memcpy overhead during continuous batching and to support incremental cache growth without full reallocation.
- Enhances continuous batching scheduler to take KV cache residency into account (hot-slot detection) and to opportunistically coalesce compatible requests without increasing SLO violations.
- Adds a runtime flag REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL (auto|flashv2|legacy) and an experimental scheduler policy `kv-aware-coalesce` that can be enabled per route.

Benchmarks (internal):
- A100-80GB long-context (8k tokens) generation: median per-token latency down 9-12% vs previous kernel, p95 down 18%.
- T4 mixed workloads: throughput +7% for small-batch streaming scenarios due to reduced memcpy and fused ops.
- Peak GPU memory reduced by ~270MB for a 7B model with 8k context compared to legacy kernels.

Compatibility and safety:
- Backwards compatible by default: kernel selector uses `auto` to prefer flashv2 when safe; falls back to legacy for models with unsupported ops or when numerical deviation crosses thresholds.
- Added a test-suite of deterministic numeric comparisons (float32/float16) and a cross-check harness that runs a representative prompt set to detect regressions.

Rollout plan:
- Canary on dedicated pools for non-sensitive tenants (2 clusters) for 48h; monitor token-level latency, p95/p99, and quality regressions via evals.
- Gradual rollout to hosted API with `kv-aware-coalesce` disabled by default; enable per-customer via feature flag.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel integration and selector changes
- [x] KV-cache layout + continuous-batching scheduler improvements
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarks and stability runs
- [x] Docs: runtime flag and rollout notes

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative around numerical tolerances; the selector will avoid FlashAttentionV2 for layers with fused custom ops that are not yet upstreamed. Follow-up PRs will add more microkernel specializations (prefetching for rotary fused path, optimized small-head attention).

release_notes: Performance: upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused-op and rotary/RoPE compatibility, improving per-token latency and reducing peak GPU memory for long-context workloads. Feature flag REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL controls runtime selection. Rollout gated behind canary and scheduler policy 'kv-aware-coalesce'.
